chapter_meta.description: Your opponent builds the solid c6-d5-e6 pawn triangle. You complete your development and prepare the central break e2-e4 to free your g2-bishop on the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: You take control of the center.
main.explanation: You put your queen's pawn in the middle of the board: your first foothold in the center.
main.hint: Start by claiming the center with a pawn.

purpose.answer: You take control of the center with your queen's pawn.
wrong: You prepare to castle quickly on the kingside.
You start an early attack on your opponent's f7-pawn.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent stops you from playing e4.
main.explanation: Your opponent develops flexibly and controls e4, so you can't easily build a full pawn center with e2-e4.

main.strategic_idea: You attack d5 and open lines for your queenside pieces.
main.explanation: Your c-pawn fights for d5 and makes room for your queenside pieces.
main.hint: Use your c-pawn to fight for d5.

purpose.answer: You fight for d5 and make room for your queenside pieces.
wrong: Your c-pawn protects your d4-pawn.
You prepare to put your queen's bishop on b2.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent supports the center and frees the dark-squared bishop.
main.explanation: Your opponent prepares ...d5 and opens the f8-bishop's path to e7, d6 or b4.

main.strategic_idea: You prepare to fianchetto your king's bishop.
main.explanation: You make room on g2 for your light-squared bishop, which will aim down the long diagonal h1-a8.
main.hint: Prepare a home for your king's bishop on the long diagonal.

purpose.answer: You make room on g2 for your bishop, aiming down the long diagonal.
wrong: You stop your opponent's bishop from giving a check on b4.
You prepare h2-h4 and an attack on your opponent's king.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent sets up a solid anchor in the center.
main.explanation: Your opponent plants a pawn in the middle of the board and blocks your long diagonal for now.

main.strategic_idea: You put your bishop on its strongest square.
main.explanation: From g2 your bishop puts long-range pressure on your opponent's queenside.
main.hint: Develop your bishop onto the long diagonal.

purpose.answer: Your bishop puts long-range pressure on your opponent's queenside.
wrong: Your bishop stops your opponent from playing ...e5.
You prepare to trade your bishop for the f6-knight.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops calmly and keeps the center closed.
main.explanation: Instead of taking your c4-pawn (the Open Catalan), your opponent keeps the pawn on d5 and gets ready to castle.

main.strategic_idea: You control d4 and e5 and get ready to castle.
main.explanation: Your knight goes to its natural square, watches d4 and e5, and clears the way for castling.
main.hint: Develop your king's knight and get ready to castle.

purpose.answer: Your knight watches d4 and e5 and clears the way for castling.
wrong: Your knight protects your c4-pawn against ...dxc4.
Your knight heads for g5 to attack the h7-pawn.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent makes the king safe before the center opens.
main.explanation: Your opponent castles short quickly, before any fight in the center begins.

main.strategic_idea: You tuck your king away behind the fianchetto.
main.explanation: Your king is safe behind the g2-bishop and the pawns, and your h1-rook joins the game.

purpose.answer: Your king gets safe behind the g2-bishop, and your rook joins the game.
wrong: You prepare to push your f-pawn to f4 and attack.
Your rook comes to f1 to put pressure on the f7-pawn.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent builds the c6-d5-e6 triangle against your g2-bishop.
main.explanation: This solid pawn triangle absorbs the pressure of your bishop on the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: You protect c4, watch the c-file and prepare e2-e4.
main.explanation: Your queen defends the c4-pawn, controls the c-file and supports your coming push e2-e4.
main.hint: Place your queen where it guards c4 and supports e4.

purpose.answer: Your queen protects c4 and supports the coming push e2-e4.
wrong: Your queen protects your d4-pawn and the d-file.
You prepare b2-b4 and a pawn attack on the queenside.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent supports d5 and keeps the center compact.
main.explanation: The knight protects the d5-point and holds your opponent's central structure together.

main.strategic_idea: You develop flexibly to support the break and keep c4 protected.
main.explanation: From d2 your knight supports e2-e4 and can recapture on c4 if needed.
main.hint: Develop your queen's knight so it supports e4 and guards c4.

purpose.answer: Your knight supports e2-e4 and can take back on c4 if needed.
wrong: You open the diagonal of your c1-bishop toward the kingside.
Your knight heads for b3 to put pressure on the c5-square.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent prepares to fianchetto the light-squared bishop.
main.explanation: Your opponent's c8-bishop is shut in by the e6-pawn, so your opponent prepares ...Bb7 to bring it to the long diagonal.

main.strategic_idea: Now you break open the center!
main.explanation: You strike in the center to open lines for your pieces and release your g2-bishop along the long diagonal.
main.hint: Your pieces are ready: strike in the center.

purpose.answer: You open the center for your pieces and free your g2-bishop.
wrong: You threaten e4-e5, and the f6-knight has nowhere to go.
You stop your opponent from ever playing the freeing ...c5.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes your c4-pawn.
main.explanation: Instead of letting you take on d5, Black captures on c4. Black gives up the d5 strongpoint, so your pawns on d4 and e4 now rule the center.

main.strategic_idea: You win the pawn back with your knight.
main.explanation: Your d2-knight recaptures and lands on an active square: from c4 it eyes d6 and e5 and puts pressure on b6.
main.hint: Win your pawn back with a knight.

purpose.answer: You win the pawn back, and your knight lands on an active square.
wrong: You come out a pawn up after the exchanges in the center.
Your knight on c4 stops your opponent from ever playing ...b5.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent finishes the fianchetto.
main.explanation: The bishop goes to the long diagonal. For now your opponent's own c6-pawn blocks it, so Black is hoping for ...c5 later to open it against your e4-pawn and your king.

main.strategic_idea: You put your rook behind your d-pawn.
main.explanation: The rook supports your d4-pawn and stands opposite the queen on d8. If Black plays ...c5, you are ready to answer with e4-e5 and gain space.
main.hint: Bring a rook behind your d-pawn.

purpose.answer: Your rook backs up your d4-pawn and faces your opponent's queen on d8.
wrong: You prepare to double your rooks on the c-file.
Your rook moves over to protect your queen on c2.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent strikes back in the center.
main.explanation: This is Black's freeing break: it attacks your d4-pawn and wants to open the long diagonal for the b7-bishop.

main.strategic_idea: You push forward and gain space.
main.explanation: Your e-pawn chases the f6-knight away from Black's kingside and takes control of d6. Black's b7-bishop now looks at your f3-knight, but your g2-bishop guards it.
main.hint: Push a pawn and chase the f6-knight.

purpose.answer: You chase the f6-knight away from the kingside and take control of d6.
wrong: You trap the f6-knight, which has no safe square left.
You prepare f2-f4 and a pawn storm on the kingside.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight jumps to a strong central square.
main.explanation: On d5 the knight blocks your d-pawn, and none of your pawns can attack it there.

main.strategic_idea: You plant your knight on d6.
main.explanation: Supported by your e5-pawn, the knight sits deep in your opponent's camp and gets in the way of Black's queen and rooks.
main.hint: Jump into the square your e5-pawn controls.

purpose.answer: Supported by e5, your knight sits deep in your opponent's camp.
wrong: Your knight protects your e5-pawn from the d7-knight.
You clear the long diagonal for your g2-bishop.

main.strategic_idea: Your opponent attacks your queen.
main.explanation: The knight hits your queen on c2 and eyes the c2 and d3 squares, so you have to move the queen.

main.strategic_idea: You keep your queen active and safe.
main.explanation: On e2 your queen is out of the knight's reach and still watches the center. If Black takes your knight with ...Bxd6, you recapture with exd6 and keep an advanced pawn in Black's camp.
main.hint: Move your queen to a safe square on the e-file.

purpose.answer: Your queen escapes the knight's attack and still watches the center.
wrong: Your queen protects your d6-knight, which needs the support.
Your queen heads for h5 to attack your opponent's h7-pawn.

line_2.explanation: It looks strange on the edge, but it has a plan: from a6 it can jump to b4 to hit your queen, or support the ...c5 break.

line_2.strategic_idea: You take the b4-square away from the knight.
line_2.explanation: Now ...Nb4 would simply lose the knight to axb4. Your a3-pawn also prepares b2-b4 later.
line_2.hint: Stop the a6-knight from jumping to b4.

purpose.answer: You take b4 away from the a6-knight and prepare b2-b4.
wrong: You prepare a4-a5 to open the a-file for your rook.
Your a-pawn steps up to protect your c4-pawn.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent strikes at your center.
line_2.explanation: Black attacks your d4-pawn. The knight on a6 supports the c5-square, so Black is ready to recapture there.

line_2.strategic_idea: You clear the center by taking on d5.
line_2.explanation: You swap your e-pawn for Black's d-pawn and open lines in the center.
line_2.hint: Take on d5 with your e-pawn.

purpose.answer: You swap your e-pawn for Black's d-pawn and open lines in the center.
wrong: You win a pawn, because d5 can't be taken back.
You stop your opponent from playing ...cxd4 for good.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent recaptures with the e-pawn.
line_2.explanation: Black now has two pawns side by side on c5 and d5. They control the center, but they can also become targets.

line_2.strategic_idea: You break up Black's pawn pair.
line_2.explanation: You take on c5. When Black recaptures with the knight, the d5-pawn has no neighbours left on the c- or e-file: it becomes an isolated pawn.
line_2.hint: Capture on c5 with your d-pawn.

purpose.answer: After the knight takes back, Black's d5-pawn is left isolated.
wrong: You open the long diagonal for your g2-bishop.
You win a pawn and keep a strong extra pawn on c5.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight finally joins the game.
line_2.explanation: From c5 the knight eyes your d3 and e4 squares. But Black's d5-pawn is now isolated, a long-term weakness you can play against.

line_2.strategic_idea: You chase the knight away and gain space.
line_2.explanation: Your b-pawn, supported by a3, attacks the c5-knight, and your c4-pawn stays protected by your queen and your d2-knight. Once the knight moves, your c1-bishop can come to b2 and aim along the long dark diagonal toward Black's king.
line_2.hint: Attack the c5-knight with a pawn.

purpose.answer: You chase the c5-knight away and gain space on the queenside.
wrong: You win the c5-knight, which has no safe square.
You open the b-file for your queen's rook.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight steps back to e6.
line_2.explanation: Attacked by your b-pawn, the knight retreats to e6. From there it watches d4 and c5 and helps protect Black's kingside.

line_2.strategic_idea: You put your bishop on the long dark diagonal.
line_2.explanation: Your bishop controls d4, the square in front of Black's isolated pawn, and already eyes the f6-knight.
line_2.hint: Put your dark-squared bishop on the long diagonal.

purpose.answer: Your bishop takes the long dark diagonal and controls d4, in front of the isolated pawn.
wrong: Your bishop protects your b4-pawn.
Your bishop attacks the isolated d5-pawn.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent takes the open c-file.
line_2.explanation: Black's rook adds pressure on your c4-pawn, which your queen and your d2-knight still protect.

line_2.strategic_idea: You plant your knight on e5.
line_2.explanation: Protected by your b2-bishop, the knight is strong on e5 and guards c4. With f3 free, your g2-bishop now sees all the way to the d5-pawn.
line_2.hint: Bring your f3-knight to a strong central square.

purpose.answer: Your knight takes a strong central square and opens the g2-bishop's view of d5.
wrong: You prepare f2-f4 and a pawn storm on the kingside.
Your knight protects your queen on c2 against the rook.

line_2.strategic_idea: Your opponent's queen joins the c-file.
line_2.explanation: The queen lines up with the rook against c4 and attacks your e5-knight, which your b2-bishop protects.

line_2.strategic_idea: You bring your last piece into play.
line_2.explanation: Your rook stands behind your queen on the c-file and meets Black's pressure there. All your pieces are in play.
line_2.hint: Bring your a1-rook to the c-file.

purpose.answer: Your rook backs up your queen on the c-file against Black's pressure there.
wrong: Your rook gets ready to swing to the kingside via c3.
Your rook protects your b4-pawn from Black's pieces.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent develops the knight to d7.
moves.explanation: A natural square, but it takes d7 away from the f6-knight, and you use that at once.

moves.strategic_idea: You push forward and chase the f6-knight.
moves.explanation: The knight's best square, d7, is taken by the other knight, so it has no good place to go. Your e5-pawn also gains space on the kingside.
moves.hint: Push your e-pawn and attack the f6-knight.

purpose.answer: You chase the f6-knight, whose best square d7 is taken, and gain space.
wrong: You open the long diagonal for your g2-bishop.
You win the f6-knight, which has no square left.

moves.strategic_idea: Your opponent's knight retreats to e8.
moves.explanation: It's passive there, but it can come back into play via c7.

moves.strategic_idea: You exchange pawns on d5.
moves.explanation: You release the tension in the center. Your pawns on d4 and e5 now stand firm, and the c-file opens.
moves.hint: Exchange your c-pawn on d5.

purpose.answer: You release the tension: your d4- and e5-pawns stand firm and the c-file opens.

moves.hint: Move your queen off the c-file to a square where it attacks something.

purpose.answer: Your queen leaves the c-file and attacks a7 and the d7-knight.
wrong: Your queen heads for h4 to attack Black's king.
Your queen attacks the e8-knight.

moves.strategic_idea: Your knight heads for the kingside.

purpose.answer: You start your play on the kingside, where Black's king is.
wrong: You open the h-file for your rook.

levels.title: The 6...c6 setup and the e2-e4 break
Test: play the 6...c6 setup from memory
Your opponent takes on c4: 9...dxc4
levels.intro: You have just played 9.e4. Now your opponent gives up the center and takes your c4-pawn.

levels.title: Your opponent breaks with ...c5
levels.intro: Your opponent finally plays the freeing ...c5. You answer by gaining space with e5 and planting a knight on d6.
key_ideas: Your knight on d6 is a thorn in Black's position. If Black takes it with ...Bxd6, recapture with exd6: the pawn on d6 keeps cramping Black.
Bring out your last pieces: your c1-bishop goes to f4 or g5, often after b3.
If Black exchanges on d4 (...cxd4), take back with a piece (Nxd4 or Rxd4) and keep control of the center.
When the c-file opens, bring your other rook to c1.

levels.title: A new branch: 7...b6
levels.intro: A new branch: this time your opponent answers 7.Qc2 with 7...b6 instead of 7...Nbd7. The first seven moves are the ones you already know.
key_ideas: Bring your bishop to b2: from there it aims along the long dark diagonal at Black's king.
Black's d5-pawn is isolated. Keep it under pressure, and use the d4-square in front of it as a home for your knight (Nd4).
Put your rooks on the open files: one on c1, one on d1.
Exchanges usually help you: the fewer pieces Black has, the weaker the isolated pawn becomes.

levels.title: The 7...b6 line to move 16
levels.intro: You know this line up to 13.b4. Now your pieces take their best squares around Black's isolated d5-pawn.
key_ideas: Your e5-knight is your best piece; keep it protected by the b2-bishop.
Keep the pressure on d5 with your g2-bishop, and bring a rook to d1 later.
If your opponent takes on c4, take back: your pieces stay more active than Black's.

levels.title: 9...Nbd7: the e5 push
levels.intro: In the 7...b6 line your opponent can also answer 9.e4 with 9...Nbd7. Now the e5 push is very strong.
key_ideas: Black plays on the queenside, you play on the kingside. That's the plan in this pawn structure.
Bring your f1-knight to e3 to attack d5, or to h2 and g4 toward Black's king.
Your e5-pawn gives you space, so keep it protected with your rook and your f3-knight.

levels.title: 7...Nbd7: two short side lines

parts.intro: After 9.e4, your opponent can take on e4 instead of c4.
key_ideas: You have more space: your c4- and d4-pawns against Black's c6 and e6.
Next, bring a rook to d1 and your bishop to f4.
If your opponent breaks with ...c5, the push d4-d5 often gains you even more space.

parts.intro: Back to move 8: your opponent can also attack your c4-pawn with 8...b5.
key_ideas: Your c5-pawn takes space and cramps Black's queenside. Keep it protected by the d4-pawn.
Open the center with e4: after the exchanges on e4 your pieces become more active.

levels.intro: In the 7...Nbd7 line your opponent has other tries than 9...dxc4. Here are two short ones.

levels.title: 8...Re8
levels.intro: Your opponent can also prepare ...e5 with 8...Re8. You strike in the center first.
key_ideas: Your pieces are more active: from b5 your knight can jump to d6, deep in Black's camp.
If Black trades on e3, take back with your queen. Even after the queens come off, Nd6 stays very strong.
Your rook on d1 owns the open d-file.

levels.title: 6...b6: the bishop goes to b7
levels.intro: Instead of 6...c6, your opponent can play 6...b6 and put the bishop on b7 before anything else.
key_ideas: Black's d5-pawn is isolated: press it with your g2-bishop, your c3-knight and your queen on the d-file.
Bring a rook to c1, on the half-open c-file, against the c5-knight.
Trades help you: the fewer pieces Black has, the weaker the isolated pawn becomes.

levels.title: 6...Ne4 and ...f5: a wall of pawns
levels.intro: Your opponent can also jump into e4 at once and support the knight with ...f5.
key_ideas: Your pawns on c4, d4 and e4 control the center, while Black's d7-bishop is hemmed in by its own pawns.
Develop your c1-bishop next and bring your last rook into play.
If your opponent takes on c4, push e4-e5 to gain space.

levels.title: 4...Bb4+: the check on b4

key_ideas: Your e5-knight is your best piece: it eyes c6, d7 and f7.
A typical plan: exchange on d5 and jump to c6. Black has to give up the b7-bishop for your knight, and your queen lands on c6.

parts.intro: If your opponent takes your e5-knight with 12...Nxe5:
key_ideas: The h5-knight is in trouble: if your opponent is careless, g3-g4 traps it.
Next, exchange on d5 and bring your b1-knight into play.

levels.intro: After 4.Bg2 your opponent can check with 4...Bb4+. You block with 5.Bd2, and the bishop goes back to e7.

levels.title: Two more ideas after 9.Rd1

parts.intro: Your opponent can develop the bishop to b7 at once:
key_ideas: You have the two bishops: open the position to make them stronger.
Develop your b1-knight to c3 next, adding pressure on d5.
Without its b7-bishop, Black has a hard time guarding the light squares.

parts.intro: Or your opponent can attack your c4-pawn with 9...Ba6:
key_ideas: Your d4-pawn is well protected by your knight, your queen and your rook.
Bring your last rook to c1 to put pressure on the c5-pawn.
Later, b3-b4 can attack Black's c5-pawn.

levels.intro: Two more ideas for your opponent after 9.Rd1.

levels.title: 5...Bxd2+: the bishops come off
levels.intro: After 4...Bb4+ 5.Bd2 your opponent can also trade the bishops at once.
key_ideas: Your queen on a4 attacks a7, so your opponent has to spend a move to save the pawn.
Your e5-pawn gives you space and keeps Black's e8-knight passive.
Trading rooks on the c-file is fine for you, because your pieces are more active.

levels.title: 8...c5: the early break

key_ideas: Black's d5-pawn is isolated: block it with your knight on d4 and attack it with your g2-bishop.
Bring your rooks to c1 and d1.
Trades help you: the fewer pieces Black has, the weaker the isolated pawn becomes.

parts.intro: Instead of 10...cxd4, your opponent can protect c5 with 10...b6:
key_ideas: The hanging pawns on c5 and d5 are your targets: press them with your queen, rooks and knights.
If Black takes on e4, take back, and the c5-pawn is isolated.
Bring your rooks to the c- and d-files.

parts.intro: Or your opponent pushes past with 10...c4:
key_ideas: Black's d5-pawn is isolated: your queen already attacks it, and your knights can use the d4-square in front of it.
Bring your rooks to the open c-file.

levels.intro: In the 5...Bxd2+ line your opponent can also strike with 8...c5 at once.

levels.title: 5...a5: the pawn-grab line

key_ideas: Black is a pawn up, but Black's queenside pieces are still at home and the queen is far away: keep your pieces active.
Put your rooks on the b- and c-files against Black's queenside.
Your knights can jump to b6 and d6, deep into Black's camp.

parts.intro: If your opponent takes your e2-pawn with 14...Nxe2+ instead:
key_ideas: Black is three pawns up, but the queen and the c3-knight are in danger: your threat is Naxc4, then Rxc3.
Black's queen has to stay careful, because your rooks can chase it along the b-file.

parts.intro: If your opponent attacks your e5-knight with 12...f6:
key_ideas: If Black takes your a1-rook, take the e4-knight. Black is behind in development and the king is still in the center, so your attack is worth more than the rook.
Your knight can jump to b6, hitting the a8-rook.

levels.intro: After 4...Bb4+ 5.Bd2 your opponent can keep the bishop on b4 with 5...a5 and grab your c4-pawn. This line is sharp: you give up pawns for active pieces, so watch for the traps.

levels.title: 5...a5 with 6...O-O
levels.intro: Your opponent can also leave your c4-pawn alone and castle with 6...O-O.
key_ideas: Black's d5-pawn is isolated: your queen on b3 already attacks it, and a knight on c3 will add pressure.
Use the d4-square in front of the isolated pawn for a knight.
Play e2-e3 to block the c5-bishop's diagonal toward f2.

levels.title: 5...Bd6: the bishop goes to d6

key_ideas: Your e5-pawn gives you space on the kingside, as in the other e5 structures of this chapter.
Keep the e5-pawn protected: your f3-knight and your d4-pawn guard it.
If the c-pawns are exchanged, your rook on c1 takes the open c-file.

parts.intro: If your opponent takes back with the queen, 10...Qxf6:
key_ideas: You traded your bishop for the knight: now play e2-e4 to open the center.
If Black plays ...e5, exchange on d5 and push e2-e4.

levels.intro: After 4...Bb4+ 5.Bd2 your opponent can also retreat the bishop to d6.

levels.title: 4...Nbd7 and ...Bd6
levels.intro: After 4.Bg2 your opponent can also develop with 4...Nbd7, then ...c6 and ...Bd6.
key_ideas: You have more space: your c4- and d4-pawns against Black's c6 and e6.
Develop your c1-bishop to f4, its most active square.

levels.title: 4...g6: a second fianchetto

key_ideas: Keep the pressure on d5: your g2-bishop, your c3-knight and your c4-pawn all attack it.
Bring a rook to d1, behind your d4-pawn.
If your opponent challenges the e5-knight with ...Nd7, you can calmly bring it back to f3.

parts.intro: If your opponent takes your e5-knight with 8...Nxe5:
key_ideas: Your e5-pawn, protected by f4, takes space and blocks the g7-bishop.
Next, exchange on d5 and push e2-e4 to build a big center.

levels.intro: After 4.Bg2 your opponent can also fianchetto the other bishop with 4...g6.

levels.title: 4...Ne4: the early knight jump
levels.intro: After 4.Bg2 your opponent can also jump into e4 at once and follow up with ...Bb4+.
key_ideas: You will win back the c4-pawn: your queen attacks it, and your knight can jump to e5 to help.
Your pawns on d4 and e3 give you a solid center.
Black's c8-bishop is still stuck behind the e6-pawn.
